internal class ScreenStoreProvider(
    private val storeFactory: StoreFactory,
    private val manager: ScreenDataManager,
    private val screen: ScreenId,
    private val stableId: String?,
    private val mainContext: CoroutineContext,
    private val restoredDraft: SavedScreenDraft? = null,
) {
    fun provide(): ScreenStore = object : ScreenStore,
        com.arkivanov.mvikotlin.core.store.Store<ScreenStore.Intent, ScreenStore.State, ScreenStore.Label> by
        storeFactory.create(
            name = "${screen.name}Store",
            initialState = ScreenStore.State(
                screen = screen,
                stableId = stableId,
                snapshot = ScreenSnapshot(selectedItemId = restoredDraft?.selectedItemId),
                draftValues = ScreenContractRegistry.contracts.getValue(screen).fields.associate { it.id to it.value } +
                    restoredDraft?.values.orEmpty().mapKeys { ScreenFieldId(it.key) },
                dirtyFields = restoredDraft?.dirtyFields.orEmpty().mapTo(mutableSetOf(), ::ScreenFieldId),
                restoredFields = restoredDraft?.values.orEmpty().keys.mapTo(mutableSetOf(), ::ScreenFieldId),
            ),
            bootstrapper = SimpleBootstrapper(Action.Observe),
            executorFactory = { ExecutorImpl() },
            reducer = ReducerImpl,
        ) {}

    private sealed interface Action { data object Observe : Action }
    private sealed interface Msg {
        data class Loaded(val snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, val protectedFields: Set<ScreenFieldId> = emptySet()) : Msg
        data class DetailLoaded(val subjectId: String, val snapshot: ScreenSnapshot) : Msg
        data class Committed(val snapshot: ScreenSnapshot) : Msg
        data class PreferenceFinished(
            val snapshot: ScreenSnapshot?, val fields: Set<ScreenFieldId>, val preserved: Set<ScreenFieldId>,
        ) : Msg
        data class StagePreviewed(val preview: com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.StageChangeProjection) : Msg
        data class PhotoPreviewed(val value: String, val photo: com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.ScreenPhoto?) : Msg
        data class Selected(val id: String) : Msg
        data class Busy(val value: Boolean) : Msg
        data class Failed(val key: TextKey) : Msg
        data class Layout(val mode: com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.LayoutMode) : Msg
        data class FieldEdited(val fieldId: ScreenFieldId, val value: String) : Msg
        data class ValidationFailed(val errors: Map<ScreenFieldId, TextKey>) : Msg
        data object DraftCancelled : Msg
    }

    private inner class ExecutorImpl :
        CoroutineExecutor<ScreenStore.Intent, Action, ScreenStore.State, Msg, ScreenStore.Label>(mainContext) {
        private var observation: Job? = null
        private var detailObservation: Job? = null
        private var photoPreview: Job? = null
        private var detailSubject: String? = null
        private val inFlight = mutableSetOf<String>()
        private val inFlightPayloads = mutableSetOf<String>()
        private val completedKeys = mutableSetOf<String>()
        private val fieldRevisions = mutableMapOf<ScreenFieldId, Long>()
        private val preferences = ArrayDeque<PreferenceRequest>()
        private var drainingPreferences = false
        private var activePreviews = 0

        private inner class PreferenceRequest(val command: ScreenCommand) {
            val invocationKeys = mutableSetOf<String>().apply { command.invocationId?.let(::add) }
            val revisions = command.arguments.keys.associate { name ->
                val id = ScreenFieldId(name)
                id to (fieldRevisions[id] ?: 0L)
            }
        }

        override fun executeAction(action: Action) { observe() }

        override fun executeIntent(intent: ScreenStore.Intent) {
            when (intent) {
                ScreenStore.Intent.Retry -> observe()
                is ScreenStore.Intent.Select -> {
                    dispatch(Msg.Selected(intent.id))
                    observeDetail(intent.id)
                }
                is ScreenStore.Intent.EditField -> {
                    fieldRevisions[intent.fieldId] = (fieldRevisions[intent.fieldId] ?: 0L) + 1
                    dispatch(Msg.FieldEdited(intent.fieldId, intent.value))
                    if (intent.fieldId.value == "photoId") previewPendingPhoto()
                }
                is ScreenStore.Intent.Submit -> submit(intent.actionId)
                ScreenStore.Intent.CancelDraft -> { dispatch(Msg.DraftCancelled); previewPendingPhoto() }
                is ScreenStore.Intent.ReportFailure -> dispatch(Msg.Failed(intent.key))
                ScreenStore.Intent.ConfirmStagePreview -> state().stagePreview?.let { executeValidated(it.command) }
                is ScreenStore.Intent.SetLayout -> dispatch(Msg.Layout(intent.mode))
                is ScreenStore.Intent.Execute -> executeValidated(intent.command)
            }
        }

        private fun submit(actionId: com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.ScreenActionId) {
            when (
                val preparation = ScreenContractRegistry.prepareCommand(
                    screen = screen,
                    actionId = actionId,
                    currentSubjectId = state().stableId ?: state().snapshot.selectedItemId,
                    draft = state().draftValues,
                )
            ) {
                is CommandPreparation.Invalid -> dispatch(Msg.ValidationFailed(preparation.errors))
                is CommandPreparation.Ready -> {
                    if (screen == ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL && preparation.command.operation in
                        com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.previewedStageOperations) {
                        previewStage(preparation.command)
                    } else if (preparation.command.destructiveOperation == null) {
                        executeValidated(preparation.command)
                    } else {
                        publish(ScreenStore.Label.ConfirmationRequested(preparation.command))
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        private fun executeValidated(command: ScreenCommand) {
            val operation = ScreenContractRegistry.contracts.getValue(screen).operations[command.operation]
            if (operation == null) {
                dispatch(Msg.ValidationFailed(mapOf(ScreenFieldId("id") to TextKey("state_error_body"))))
                return
            }
            if (!operation.itemTargeted) {
                execute(command)
                return
            }
            val draft = command.arguments.mapKeys { (name, _) -> ScreenFieldId(name) }
            when (
                val preparation = ScreenContractRegistry.prepareCommand(
                    screen = screen,
                    actionId = com.sedsoftware.sproutpace.component.ScreenActionId(command.operation),
                    currentSubjectId = command.subjectId,
                    draft = draft,
                )
            ) {
                is CommandPreparation.Invalid -> dispatch(Msg.ValidationFailed(preparation.errors))
                is CommandPreparation.Ready -> {
                    val exactTarget = state().snapshot.items.any { item ->
                        item.commands.any { target ->
                            target.operation == command.operation && target.subjectId == command.subjectId
                        }
                    }
                    if (operation.itemTargeted && !exactTarget) {
                        dispatch(Msg.ValidationFailed(mapOf(ScreenFieldId("id") to TextKey("state_error_body"))))
                    } else if (
                        preparation.command.operation != command.operation ||
                        preparation.command.subjectId != command.subjectId ||
                        preparation.command.arguments != command.arguments
                    ) {
                        dispatch(Msg.ValidationFailed(mapOf(ScreenFieldId("id") to TextKey("state_error_body"))))
                    } else {
                        execute(command)
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        private fun previewStage(command: ScreenCommand) {
            val draft = state().draftValues
            scope.launch {
                activePreviews += 1
                dispatch(Msg.Busy(true))
                try {
                    manager.previewStage(command).unwrap(
                        onSuccess = { if (state().draftValues == draft) dispatch(Msg.StagePreviewed(it)) },
                        onFailure = { dispatch(Msg.Failed(TextKey("error_operation_failed"))) },
                    )
                } finally {
                    activePreviews -= 1
                    dispatchBusy()
                }
            }
        }

        private fun observe() {
            observation?.cancel()

                manager.watch(screen, stableId).collectLatest {
                    dispatch(Msg.Loaded(it, preferences.flatMap { request -> request.revisions.keys }.toSet()))
                    previewPendingPhoto()
                    observeDetail(state().snapshot.selectedItemId)
                }
            }
        }

            photoPreview = scope.launch {

# SCREEN-011 - Settings

Linked flows: FLOW-001, FLOW-009, FLOW-010, FLOW-011, FLOW-012  
Linked requirements: REQ-001, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012

## Purpose and hierarchy

Provide stable entry points for appearance, notifications, zones, tray presets, data portability, applicable advertising privacy, crash reporting, privacy policy, and destructive reset.

## States

- Content grouped by Growing setup, Preferences, Privacy, and Data.
- Crash reporting effective/failed initialization state.
- Advertising consent row appears only while fresh applicability requires management.
- Notification permission denied summary.
- Local loading/error only where a preference write is in progress; offline does not block settings.

## Actions and iconography

Navigation rows open SCREEN-012-016 and SCREEN-014. Theme uses a choice control; Crashlytics uses an independent switch with explanatory text. Delete all data is a destructive labeled action. Standard settings-category icons have text labels.

## Text layout expectations

Each row has a concise title and optional state summary. Crashlytics copy says disabling affects future collection, not already transmitted reports. At 200% trailing switches remain aligned without squeezing titles into unusable columns.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact is one grouped list; expanded uses list-detail for selected settings destination. Switch labels expose current state, rows have unique accessible names, and keyboard focus is visible. Scaffold/navigation own safe areas once.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard theme, notification, zone, tray, backup, privacy, crash-reporting, policy, chevron, and delete icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

EN compact light/dark; RU 200%; notification denied; consent-management row shown/hidden; Crashlytics off and init-failed; expanded list-detail; destructive reset confirmation.

# SCREEN-012 - Zones

Linked flows: FLOW-001, FLOW-003, FLOW-004, FLOW-005  
Linked requirements: REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005

## Purpose and hierarchy

Manage named Light and Dark growing zones with positive integer capacity and understandable occupied/available counts.

## States

- Content list with type, capacity, occupancy, and conflicts.
- Empty setup state with Add zone.
- Add/edit validation for blank name, duplicate identity handling, invalid capacity, and capacity below real occupancy.
- Delete blocked or explained when referenced; local save failure preserves input.
- Offline: fully available.

## Actions and iconography

Add zone is primary; rows expose Edit and Delete. Capacity conflict offers reassign, increase capacity, or keep affected future batches needing resolution. Use standard light, dark/covered, capacity, add, edit, delete, and warning icons.

## Text layout expectations

Zone type is always stated in text. Occupancy reads as localized `occupied of capacity`; names wrap. Numeric validation specifies positive whole places, not area or geometry.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact navigates list to editor; expanded uses list-detail. Counters have semantic descriptions, and warnings use icon plus text. Keyboard users can reach every row action without long press or swipe.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard light, covered/dark, capacity, add, edit, delete, and warning icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Light/dark zones with occupancy; empty; add/edit; invalid capacity; referenced delete; future conflict; RU 200%; expanded list-detail; offline.

# SCREEN-013 - Tray sizes

Linked flows: FLOW-001, FLOW-004  
Linked requirements: REQ-001, REQ-004

## Purpose and hierarchy

Manage reusable metric tray-size presets as rectangular width ? length or circular diameter, without tracking empty tray inventory.

## States

- Content list grouped or labeled by shape.
- Empty setup state with Add preset.
- Add/edit validation for blank name and non-positive dimensions.
- Referenced delete confirmation explains snapshots remain intact.
- Local save error; offline fully available.

## Actions and iconography

Add preset is primary; rows expose Edit and Delete. Shape uses radio/connected selection with explicit Rectangle/Circle labels. Standard tray, rectangle, circle, add, edit, and delete icons supplement text.

## Text layout expectations

Every number includes `cm`; multiplication sign and diameter label are localized safely. Names wrap and dimensions remain readable at 200% without fixed-width fields.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact is list-to-editor; expanded is list-detail. Shape is announced by name rather than inferred from art. Numeric fields support keyboard entry and clear error associations. One scaffold owns insets.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard tray, rectangle, circle, add, edit, delete, and save icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Mixed preset list light/dark; empty; rectangle editor; circle editor; invalid values; referenced delete; RU 200%; long name; expanded list-detail.

# SCREEN-014 - Backup and restore

Linked flows: FLOW-009  
Linked requirements: REQ-009

## Purpose and hierarchy

Create a complete local backup, preview and confirm replacement restore, export history CSV, or reach destructive reset with explicit consequences.

## States

- Idle action list.
- Backup/CSV destination selection and measurable progress.
- Valid restore preview with version, date, counts, photos, and replacement warning.
- Invalid/unsupported archive error with no mutation.
- Restore/export success or failure; cancelled picker returns to idle.

## Actions and iconography

Create backup, Restore backup, Export history CSV, and Delete all data are labeled rows/buttons. Confirm restore and delete use destructive confirmation; system pickers own file browsing. Use standard backup, restore, file, table, warning, and delete icons.

## Text layout expectations

File metadata and counts wrap; technical format errors are translated into actionable copy without leaking paths unnecessarily. Replacement and no-merge behavior is stated before confirmation. Progress labels do not rely on animation alone.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact pushes restore preview as a full page; expanded uses a supporting pane. Progress is announced without excessive updates. Focus moves to preview/error heading after picker return. Safe areas are consumed once.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard backup, restore, document, table/export, warning, delete, and close icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Idle light/dark; valid preview; replacement confirmation; invalid archive; in-progress export; failed write; success; RU 200%; expanded preview; delete-all confirmation.

# SCREEN-015 - Advertising privacy

Linked flows: FLOW-010  
Linked requirements: REQ-010

## Purpose and hierarchy

Collect or manage consent only when a fresh response from the fixed privacy-region endpoint says protected-region consent is required.

## States

- First decision: neutral explanation, Accept, Decline, and Privacy policy.
- Previously accepted: withdrawal action and current policy/version context.
- Previously declined: retained state and policy link.
- Endpoint stale/unavailable: no consent guess and no ads; decision controls wait for fresh applicability.
- Policy version changed: prior choice is unresolved and a new decision is shown.

## Actions and iconography

Accept and Decline have equal clarity and neither uses deceptive prominence. Privacy policy opens the configured destination. Withdraw is explicit and confirmed only if needed to explain immediate effect. Use standard privacy, policy/link, accept, decline, and warning icons with labels.

## Text layout expectations

Copy distinguishes app consent choice from operating-system controls and avoids legal claims beyond supplied policy text. Endpoint/policy metadata is secondary. At 200%, buttons stack and full labels remain visible.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact is a full-screen decision; expanded uses a bounded supporting surface, never a tiny modal. Initial focus is on the heading, actions have equal semantic weight, and back does not imply consent. One safe-area owner applies.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard privacy, policy/link, accept, decline, withdraw, and warning icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

First decision EN/RU light/dark; RU 200%; accepted with withdrawal; declined; stale endpoint; endpoint failure; changed policy version; expanded decision surface.

# SCREEN-016 - Notifications

Linked flows: FLOW-001, FLOW-003  
Linked requirements: REQ-001, REQ-003

## Purpose and hierarchy

Configure the 09:00-local daily work summary, optional separate soak target reminder, and recover from notification permission denial without weakening Today as the source of truth.

## States

- Summary enabled/disabled with local time selection; default 09:00.
- Soak reminder enabled/disabled according to batch applicability.
- Runtime permission not requested, granted, denied, or permanently denied.
- Scheduled summary contains work / no work, where no-work means no notification.
- Scheduling error exposes recovery while in-app actions remain intact.

## Actions and iconography

Independent switches control summary and soak reminders; time picker changes summary time. Request permission and Open system settings are labeled contextual actions. Use standard notification, notification-off, time, soak, and settings icons.

## Text layout expectations

Explain best-effort target timing and that SproutPace does not request exact-alarm special access. Permission copy says Today remains current. Times use locale conventions; at 200% state summaries wrap below switches.

## Responsive, accessibility, and insets

Compact and expanded both use a bounded settings column. Switches expose state and consequence, time picker has manual entry, and permission changes are announced. Scaffold owns insets once.

## Allowed ad slots

None.

## Asset requirements

Standard notification, notification-off, time, soak, system-settings, and warning icons.

## Preview and golden matrix

Enabled at 09:00 light/dark; disabled; permission not requested/denied/permanently denied; soak applicable; schedule error; RU 200%; expanded settings; offline.

# Data

## Local persistence

Use a shared Kotlin Multiplatform database for relational product data, typed Multiplatform Settings for small preferences/privacy caches, and private app storage for imported observation photos. Managers own persistence boundaries; Stores never call database or platform APIs directly.

Expected local records include:

- grow zones and capacity;
- tray-size presets;
- personal recipes and recipe stages;
- grow batches with immutable recipe, tray, substrate, culture, supplier/cultivar/lot, and zone-name snapshots;
- stage events and derived scheduled actions;
- harvest plans and suggestions;
- observations and photo references;
- terminal outcomes and optional actual mass;
- notification preferences and stable scheduled IDs;
- theme preference;
- Crashlytics collection preference;
- one versioned advertising privacy payload containing only the minimal endpoint response, current choice, and matching policy version.

Use stable language-neutral IDs and foreign keys. Do not persist resolved built-in translations.

## Managed operations

`app-spec.json#managedEntities` is authoritative. Important consequences:

- Deleting zones, presets, or recipes does not erase immutable batch snapshots.
- Delete and terminal batch outcomes are different operations.
- Backup archives are immutable external files; create another archive rather than updating one.
- Ad-consent withdrawal is an update, not deletion.
- Crash reporting always has a default-on release preference and is disabled by updating that preference.

## Built-in catalog

Ship catalog content as versioned, deterministic local seed/reference data with stable culture IDs and string-resource keys. Recommended structure:

- `catalogVersion`: a simple monotonic content version;
- `reviewedOn`: content update date;
- culture ID and scientific/common-name resource keys;
- source URL/title metadata;
- stage applicability and duration ranges;
- blackout/weight and presoak flags/ranges;
- metric density input and its source/version;
- substrate/lighting notes as resource keys;
- safety note keys;
- illustration resource name.

Updating the catalog needs no external approval, signature, or attestation. It must change the version/date, preserve IDs where semantics are unchanged, document sources, and pass QG-011. A breaking identity change requires an explicit migration.

## Localized text storage

The complete English key set lives in `shared/compose/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings.xml`; Russian lives in `values-ru/strings.xml`. Catalog seed data and database rows contain only IDs/resource keys. Resolve keys to generated `Res.string.*` accessors at the presentation boundary.

User-authored recipe names, supplier/lot notes, observations, and batch notes are stored verbatim and are not resource strings. Native-only Android/iOS permission and platform text uses native localized resources with English base and Russian addition.

## Backup archive

The full backup is a versioned local archive selected through the platform document provider. It contains:

- a manifest with schema/version and counts;
- all product records and stable relationships;
- app-owned observation photos with integrity metadata;
- user preferences needed to restore product behavior;
- no Crashlytics server data, advertising SDK cache, detected country/IP, advertising ID, or secrets.

Before restore, parse and validate the complete archive, show a localized preview, and require explicit replacement confirmation. Replacement is transactional: stage files and database content, commit both, then rebuild only future reminders. Invalid or unsupported archives leave existing data and files untouched. Restoring the same archive again replaces rather than merges, so it cannot duplicate records.

CSV export contains a localized or documented stable header contract for batch history, culture/recipe identity, relevant dates, outcome, actual mass, and user notes as appropriate. It excludes photographs and does not serve as a restorable backup.

## Remote APIs

### Privacy-region endpoint

Use `GET https://168.222.252.178/v1/privacy/region` exactly as defined by the monetization contract. Send no query parameters or user/install/location identifiers. Accept only strict schema 1 JSON with exact JSON content type, a supported policy version string, and `expiresAt` no more than 72 hours ahead. Reject redirects, non-200 responses, malformed/oversized/non-UTF-8 bodies, unknown schema, stale/overlong expiry, and transport failures.

The endpoint is an accepted shared service. Do not create a backend, alternative service, live qualification, readiness attestation, or endpoint-specific release gate.

### Yandex Ads

Send only the configured ad-unit ID unless a later approved privacy inventory adds something. No product data, notes, schedules, culture choices, photos, user ID, location, or account data enters an ad request. Debug/test uses test IDs; previews and automated tests make no real requests.

### Firebase Crashlytics

Crashlytics is configured separately for Android and iOS release/release-candidate builds. Do not add Firebase Analytics. Do not set a user ID or log user-authored text, crop/recipe selections, schedules, photos, advertising state, or breadcrumbs. Allowed context is limited to app version, platform/build, stack traces, ANR/fatal data, selected technical non-fatals, and reviewed non-PII technical keys.

The release default is collection enabled. The persisted user toggle disables or re-enables future collection according to the platform SDK contract. Local reset does not claim to delete reports already sent to Firebase.

## Offline and cache behavior

- Core database, catalog, photos, plan, history, backup, export, and Settings work offline.
- A valid privacy-region response may be cached only until its accepted expiry, clamped to 72 hours.
- Missing/stale privacy data disables ads for that launch; it does not delay app startup or core screens.
- Crash reports may remain queued by the native SDK contract, but upload never blocks the UI.
- There is no cloud sync, merge policy, login token, or remote product cache.

## Retention and erasure

Product data remains until the user deletes individual records, uses Delete all local data, clears app storage, or uninstalls. Delete all removes database rows, private photos, product/settings state, ad-consent payload, and scheduled reminders, then returns to first run. It explains that previously sent Crashlytics reports and externally saved backup/CSV files are not deleted.

    @Test fun ac072Ac073_publicObservationEditAndConfirmedDeletePreserveOtherTimelineAndPhotosAfterReopen() = runTest {
        withPublicWorkspace { directory, preferences ->
            val retained = PublicProductionFixture(directory, preferences).use { fixture ->
                fixture.seed()
                attachObservation(fixture, "observation-a", "Original", byteArrayOf(1, 2))
                attachObservation(fixture, "observation-b", "Other", byteArrayOf(3, 4))
                advanceUntilIdle()
                val before = fixture.database.snapshot().observations.associateBy { it.id.value }
                val originalPhoto = requireNotNull(before.getValue("observation-a").photoId)
                val peerPhoto = requireNotNull(before.getValue("observation-b").photoId)
                fixture.save(ScreenId.OBSERVATION_EDITOR, "observation-a", "save-observation", mapOf(
                    "text" to "Edited \"����\"", "occurredAt" to "2026-10-10T11:30:00Z"))
                advanceUntilIdle()
                val edited = fixture.database.snapshot().observations.single { it.id.value == "observation-a" }
                assertEquals(ObservationId("observation-a"), edited.id)
                assertEquals("Edited \"����\"", edited.text)
                assertEquals(Instant.parse("2026-10-10T11:30:00Z"), edited.occurredAt)
                assertEquals(originalPhoto, edited.photoId)
                assertContentEquals(byteArrayOf(1, 2), fixture.files.read(originalPhoto))
                assertEquals(before.getValue("observation-b"), fixture.database.snapshot().observations.single { it.id.value == "observation-b" })
                fixture.open(ScreenId.OBSERVATION_EDITOR, "observation-a")
                fixture.submit("delete-observation", confirm = false)
                assertEquals(DestructiveOperation.DELETE_OBSERVATION, fixture.root.confirmation.value.child?.configuration?.destructiveOperation)
                assertEquals(2, fixture.database.snapshot().observations.size)
                assertNotNull(fixture.files.read(originalPhoto))
                fixture.root.dismissConfirmation()
                assertEquals(2, fixture.database.snapshot().observations.size)
                fixture.submit("delete-observation")
                advanceUntilIdle()
                assertNull(fixture.files.read(originalPhoto))
                assertContentEquals(byteArrayOf(3, 4), fixture.files.read(peerPhoto))
                assertEquals(listOf(before.getValue("observation-b")), fixture.database.snapshot().observations)
                fixture.backup.createArchive()
            }
            PublicProductionFixture(directory, preferences).use { reopened ->
                assertEquals(retained, reopened.backup.createArchive())
                reopened.open(ScreenId.OBSERVATION_EDITOR, "observation-b")
                assertEquals("Other", reopened.field("text"))
                assertEquals(1, reopened.files.exportAll().size)
            }
        }
    }

function Invoke-Adb {
    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)][string[]]$Arguments)
    $previousErrorActionPreference = $ErrorActionPreference
    $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
    $output = & $adb -s $AvdSerial @Arguments 2>&1
    $ErrorActionPreference = $previousErrorActionPreference
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "ADB failed: $($Arguments -join ' ')`n$($output -join "`n")"
    }
    return ($output -join "`n")
}

function Dump-Ui {
    param([string]$Name)
    $remote = "/sdcard/sproutpace-$Name.xml"
    Invoke-Adb shell uiautomator dump $remote | Out-Null
    $local = Join-Path $reportDirectory "$Name.xml"
    Invoke-Adb pull $remote $local | Out-Null
    return [xml](Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $local)
}

function Nodes {
    param([xml]$Document)
    return @($Document.SelectNodes("//node"))
}

function Find-Node {
    param(
        [xml]$Document,
        [string]$Text = "",
        [string]$ContentDescription = "",
        [string]$ClassName = "",
        [int]$Index = 0
    )
    $matches = @(Nodes $Document | Where-Object {
        ($Text -eq "" -or $_.GetAttribute("text") -eq $Text) -and
        ($ContentDescription -eq "" -or $_.GetAttribute("content-desc") -eq $ContentDescription) -and
        ($ClassName -eq "" -or $_.GetAttribute("class") -eq $ClassName)
    })
    $node = if ($Index -lt $matches.Count) { $matches[$Index] } else { $null }
    if ($null -eq $node) {
        $description = if ($Text) { "text '$Text'" } elseif ($ContentDescription) {
            "content description '$ContentDescription'"
        } else { "class '$ClassName' at index $Index" }
        throw "Missing UI node with $description"
    }
    return $node
}

function Find-ClickableAncestor {
    param([System.Xml.XmlNode]$Node)
    $candidate = $Node
    while ($null -ne $candidate -and $candidate.Name -eq "node") {
        if ($candidate.GetAttribute("clickable") -eq "true") { return $candidate }
        $candidate = $candidate.ParentNode
    }
    throw "Node has no clickable ancestor"
}

function Bounds {
    param([System.Xml.XmlNode]$Node)
    $match = [regex]::Match($Node.GetAttribute("bounds"), '^\[(\d+),(\d+)\]\[(\d+),(\d+)\]$')
    if (-not $match.Success) { throw "Invalid node bounds: $($Node.GetAttribute('bounds'))" }
    return @(
        [int]$match.Groups[1].Value,
        [int]$match.Groups[2].Value,
        [int]$match.Groups[3].Value,
        [int]$match.Groups[4].Value
    )
}

function Tap-Node {
    param([System.Xml.XmlNode]$Node)
    $clickable = Find-ClickableAncestor $Node
    $bounds = Bounds $clickable
    Invoke-Adb shell input tap ([int](($bounds[0] + $bounds[2]) / 2)) ([int](($bounds[1] + $bounds[3]) / 2)) | Out-Null
}

function Assert-MinimumTarget {
    param(
        [System.Xml.XmlNode]$Node,
        [double]$MinimumPixels,
        [string]$Label
    )
    $clickable = Find-ClickableAncestor $Node
    $bounds = Bounds $clickable
    $width = $bounds[2] - $bounds[0]
    $height = $bounds[3] - $bounds[1]
    if ($width -lt $MinimumPixels -or $height -lt $MinimumPixels) {
        throw "$Label target is ${width}x${height}px; expected at least $([math]::Ceiling($MinimumPixels))px"
    }
}

function Assert-NodeOnScreen {
    param(
        [System.Xml.XmlNode]$Node,
        [int]$ScreenWidth,
        [int]$ScreenHeight,
        [string]$Label
    )
    $bounds = Bounds $Node
    if ($bounds[0] -lt 0 -or $bounds[1] -lt 0 -or $bounds[2] -gt $ScreenWidth -or
        $bounds[3] -gt $ScreenHeight -or $bounds[2] -le $bounds[0] -or $bounds[3] -le $bounds[1]) {
        throw "$Label is clipped or outside the screen: $($Node.GetAttribute('bounds'))"
    }
}

    param(

    for ($tabIndex = 1; $tabIndex -le $MaximumTabs; $tabIndex += 1) {

    throw "Keyboard Tab could not reach $description"
}

/** Composes the real router and Stores; only the external region, network and SDK/view ports record calls. */
class AdvertisingRootProductionTest {
    private var onFrame: () -> Unit = {}
    private var rootDiagnostic: () -> String = { "" }
    private var lastImage: BufferedImage? = null
    @get:Rule val paparazzi = Paparazzi(
        environment = detectEnvironment().copy(compileSdkVersion = 37),
        deviceConfig = DeviceConfig.PIXEL_5.copy(screenHeight = 6000),
        snapshotHandler = object : SnapshotHandler {
            override fun newFrameHandler(snapshot: Snapshot, frameCount: Int, fps: Int) = object : SnapshotHandler.FrameHandler {
                override fun handle(image: BufferedImage) { lastImage = image; onFrame() }
                override fun close() = Unit

    @Test
    fun realConsentAcceptWithdrawalAndChangedPolicyGateTheOwnedBanner() = runTest {
        withPublicWorkspace { directory, preferences ->
            PublicProductionFixture(directory, preferences, initialScreen = ScreenId.CATALOG,
                now = { kotlinx.datetime.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(System.currentTimeMillis()) }).use { fixture ->
                fixture.seed()
                val before = fixture.database.snapshot()
                val runtime = ControllerRuntime(fixture.settings)
                val root = RuntimeRoot(fixture.root, runtime)
                val view = rootView(root)
                var reconnectedFrames = 0
                play(view, listOf(
                    {
                        if (fixture.model().screen != ScreenId.ADVERTISING_PRIVACY) false else {
                            assertTrue(runtime.events.isEmpty(), "No SDK call may precede the actual consent decision")
                            view.clickTag("action-accept-advertising-consent")
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (runtime.created != 1 || view.tagged("inline-ad").isEmpty()) false else {
                            assertEquals(ScreenId.CATALOG, fixture.model().screen)
                            assertEquals(ConsentChoice.ACCEPTED, fixture.settings.privacyState.value?.choice)
                            assertEquals(listOf("consent:true", "initialize", "load"), runtime.events)
                            assertEquals(1, view.tagged("inline-ad").size)
                            view.assertSlotBetween(fixture.model().toUiState().items, 4)
                            runtime.networkAvailable.value = false
                            true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (runtime.disposed != 1 || view.tagged("inline-ad").isNotEmpty()) false else {
                            runtime.networkAvailable.value = true
                            true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        reconnectedFrames += 1
                        if (reconnectedFrames < 4) false else {
                            assertEquals(1, runtime.created, "Reconnect must not load a second banner during the same visit")
                            fixture.dispatch(UiAction.Navigate(UiScreen.TODAY))
                            true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (view.tagged("screen-today").isEmpty()) false else {
                            fixture.dispatch(UiAction.Navigate(UiScreen.CATALOG)); true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (runtime.created != 2 || view.tagged("inline-ad").isEmpty()) false else {
                            assertEquals(1, runtime.disposed)
                            fixture.dispatch(UiAction.Navigate(UiScreen.SETTINGS))
                            true
                        }
                    },
                    { view.clickTag("settings-open-advertising-privacy") },
                    { view.clickTag("action-withdraw-advertising-consent") },
                    {
                        val withdrawn = org.jetbrains.compose.resources.getString(strictTextResource("privacy_withdrawn"))
                        val statusVisible = view.nodes().any { node ->
                            node.config.getOrNull(SemanticsProperties.Text)?.any { it.text == withdrawn } == true
                        }
                        if (fixture.settings.privacyState.value?.choice != ConsentChoice.WITHDRAWN || !statusVisible) false else {
                            assertEquals(listOf("consent:false", "stop"), runtime.events.takeLast(2))
                            assertEquals(2, runtime.disposed, "Each owned banner is disposed once when its real view leaves")
                            fixture.dispatch(UiAction.Navigate(UiScreen.CATALOG))
                            true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (fixture.model().screen != ScreenId.CATALOG || view.tagged("screen-catalog").isEmpty()) false else {
                            assertEquals(2, runtime.created)
                            runtime.policy = "policy-2"
                            fixture.settings.setPrivacyState(assertNotNull(fixture.settings.privacyState.value).copy(
                                fetchedAtEpochMillis = runtime.now - 2_000, expiresAtEpochMillis = runtime.now - 1))
                            fixture.dispatch(UiAction.Navigate(UiScreen.TODAY))
                            true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (view.tagged("screen-today").isEmpty()) false else {
                            fixture.dispatch(UiAction.Navigate(UiScreen.CATALOG)); true
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (fixture.model().screen != ScreenId.ADVERTISING_PRIVACY) false else {
                            assertEquals("policy-2", fixture.settings.privacyState.value?.policyVersion)
                            assertEquals(ConsentChoice.UNDECIDED, fixture.settings.privacyState.value?.choice)
                            assertEquals(2, runtime.created)
                            view.clickTag("action-decline-advertising-consent")
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        if (fixture.model().screen != ScreenId.CATALOG) false else {
                            assertEquals(before, fixture.database.snapshot())
                            assertEquals(ConsentChoice.DECLINED, fixture.settings.privacyState.value?.choice)
                            assertEquals(2, runtime.created)
                            assertTrue(view.tagged("inline-ad").isEmpty())
                            true
                        }
                    },
                ))
                assertEquals(2, runtime.created)
            }
        }
    }

# Production UI redesign review - 2026-09-27

Status: Accepted

Blocking findings: none

## Evidence reviewed

- Approved product behavior: `spec/app-spec.json` and `spec/screens/SCREEN-001.md` through `SCREEN-016.md`.
- Research baseline: [Lazyweb cross-screen product UI research](https://www.lazyweb.com/agentic-search/0d8da7b5-4c89-4516-99bb-ce0e2b7d76ba).
- Visual evidence: all 78 tracked Paparazzi goldens, including light, dark, expanded, error/conflict/permission states, and RU at 200% font scale.
- Runtime evidence: `.vibe/scripts/run-android-ui-smoke.ps1` on a Pixel 8 AVD at 420 dpi. It verifies the accessibility tree, 48dp targets, keyboard focus and activation, notification permission denial/recovery, Android system-settings recovery, process restart, manual time entry, save completion, and persistence after restart.
- Shared system: `SproutPaceTypography`, `SproutPaceShapes`, Material color roles, adaptive navigation, and common action/form presentation in `shared/compose`.

## Screen-by-screen closure

| Screen | Review result | Final disposition |
|---|---|---|
| SCREEN-001 - First run | Accepted | Keeps the approved setup and catalog escape route; the supporting visual is calm and no technical identifiers are exposed. |
| SCREEN-002 - Today | Accepted | One clear next action, quieter supporting state, meaningful empty state, and stable Settings access. |
| SCREEN-003 - Trays | Accepted | Planned/Active/History remain peer tabs with adaptive list-detail behavior and category-specific empty states. |
| SCREEN-004 - Batch editor | Accepted | The approved staged form remains intact; fields, capacity feedback, and primary completion action share the common form system. |
| SCREEN-005 - Batch detail | Accepted | Stage progression stays dominant; expected/actual/skipped/fixed meaning is not color-only, and only lifecycle-applicable actions are exposed for planned, soaking, active, ready, and terminal states. |
| SCREEN-006 - Plan | Accepted | The linear rhythm and conflict model remain legible without low-value dashboard counters or a misleading calendar metaphor. |
| SCREEN-007 - Catalog | Accepted | Search is a first-class rounded Material field; image-led cards retain provenance, offline behavior, and adaptive columns. |
| SCREEN-008 - Recipe | Accepted | Stage content and provenance remain available without generic section labels or repeated summaries. |
| SCREEN-009 - Observation | Accepted | Date, note, and private photo actions remain; storage IDs and redundant helper cards are absent. |
| SCREEN-010 - Close batch | Accepted | Outcome selection is the focus and one Save outcome action replaces redundant outcome shortcut buttons. |
| SCREEN-011 - Settings | Accepted | Quiet grouped rows, readable switch labels, and clear privacy/data consequences hold at RU 200% scale. |
| SCREEN-012 - Zones | Accepted | Capacity and conflict meaning remain visible; record IDs are hidden and destructive actions use low-emphasis error treatment. |
| SCREEN-013 - Tray sizes | Accepted | Metric dimensions and snapshot-safe consequences remain clear without record IDs or generic headings. |
| SCREEN-014 - Backup/restore | Accepted | Action-led rows avoid duplicate full-width actions; restore metadata appears only when it changes the decision. |
| SCREEN-015 - Advertising privacy | Accepted | Neutral context and equally understandable consent choices are preserved; declining remains a complete path. |
| SCREEN-016 - Notifications | Accepted | Editable switches/time are shown once, permission recovery is explicit, and device smoke proves denial, settings recovery, manual input, save, and restart persistence. |

## Cross-screen conclusions

- The common typography and shape scale are applied at the Material theme boundary; screens do not define competing type systems.
- Primary, secondary, outlined, and destructive actions now communicate hierarchy consistently.
- Generic Items/Details/Actions headings, technical IDs, duplicate Backup actions, duplicate Close batch outcomes, and repeated notification summaries were removed.
- Batch Detail now derives its primary and secondary actions from the real batch state: start/confirm/skip/undo/overflow/close/repeat/mass actions appear only when their domain preconditions hold.
- Current goldens show no clipping or overlap in the reviewed compact, expanded, dark, and RU/200% states.
- The redesign changes presentation, not approved product scope or business rules.

## Release boundary

This review closes the product-design surface, not every external release gate. Publication is not requested in this delivery, so store publication/signing, production Firebase symbolication, production Yandex ad-device validation, and store/privacy disclosure publication are inactive until their required external projects, credentials, policy URL, and explicit publication request exist. Safe development defaults remain required by the project guide. macOS Simulator execution and `xcodebuild` remain CI/macOS-only evidence and must not be reported as locally passed on Windows.

class CommandInvocationIntegrationTest {
    @Test
    fun pauseResumePauseResumeIsNotSuppressedByAnEarlierInvocation() = runTest {
        withManager { manager, database ->
            manager.execute(ScreenId.PLAN, prepared(ScreenId.PLAN, "save-plan", "plan", mapOf(
                "cadenceDays" to "3", "cultureIds" to "pea", "mode" to "continuous_queue",
            ))).getOrThrow()
            repeat(2) {
                manager.execute(ScreenId.PLAN, prepared(ScreenId.PLAN, "pause-plan", "plan")).getOrThrow()
                assertEquals(true, database.snapshot().plans.single().paused)
                manager.execute(ScreenId.PLAN, prepared(ScreenId.PLAN, "resume-plan", "plan")).getOrThrow()
                assertEquals(false, database.snapshot().plans.single().paused)
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun newEditsCanReturnToEarlierValuesWhileSameInvocationRemainsIdempotent() = runTest {
        withManager { manager, database ->
            listOf("A", "B", "A").forEach { name ->
                val command = prepared(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, "save-tray-size", "tray", mapOf(
                    "name" to name, "shape" to "rectangle", "widthCm" to "25.4", "lengthCm" to "50.8",
                ))
                manager.execute(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, command).getOrThrow()
                manager.execute(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, command).getOrThrow()
                assertEquals(name, database.snapshot().trayPresets.single().name)
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun transitionUndoTransitionUndoUsesNewInvocationsButRepeatedCallbacksDoNotMutate() = runTest {
        withManager { manager, database ->
            manager.execute(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, prepared(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, "save-tray-size", "tray", mapOf(
                "name" to "Tray", "shape" to "rectangle", "widthCm" to "25.4", "lengthCm" to "50.8",
            ))).getOrThrow()
            val save = prepared(ScreenId.BATCH_EDITOR, "save-batch", "batch", mapOf(
                "cultureId" to "pea", "trayId" to "tray", "substrate" to "Coco",
                "plannedSowDate" to "2026-10-10", "timeZoneId" to "UTC",
            ))
            manager.execute(ScreenId.BATCH_EDITOR, save).getOrThrow()
            manager.execute(ScreenId.BATCH_EDITOR, save).getOrThrow()
            assertEquals(1, database.snapshot().batches.size)
            repeat(2) {
                val transition = prepared(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, "start-soaking", "batch", mapOf(
                    "eventId" to "same-event", "occurredAt" to "2026-10-10T09:00:00Z",
                ))
                manager.execute(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, transition).getOrThrow()
                val afterTransition = database.snapshot().batches.single()
                assertEquals(BatchState.SOAKING, afterTransition.state)
                manager.execute(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, transition).getOrThrow()
                assertEquals(afterTransition, database.snapshot().batches.single())
                val undo = prepared(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, "undo-stage", "batch")
                manager.execute(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, undo).getOrThrow()
                val afterUndo = database.snapshot().batches.single()
                assertEquals(BatchState.PLANNED, afterUndo.state)
                manager.execute(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, undo).getOrThrow()
                assertEquals(afterUndo, database.snapshot().batches.single())
            }
        }

    @Test
    fun preparationSeparatesInvocationFromPayloadAndCopyKeepsInvocation() {
        val first = prepared(ScreenId.SETTINGS, "set-theme", null, mapOf("theme" to "dark"))
        val second = prepared(ScreenId.SETTINGS, "set-theme", null, mapOf("theme" to "dark"))
        assertEquals(first.deduplicationKey, second.deduplicationKey)
        assertNotEquals(first.executionKey, second.executionKey)
        assertEquals(first.executionKey, first.copy().executionKey)
    }

    @Test
    fun reusingInvocationWithDifferentPayloadIsRejectedWithoutMutation() = runTest {
        withManager { manager, database ->
            val command = prepared(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, "save-tray-size", "tray", mapOf(
                "name" to "Original", "shape" to "rectangle", "widthCm" to "25.4", "lengthCm" to "50.8",
            ))
            manager.execute(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES, command).getOrThrow()
            val before = database.snapshot()
            assertTrue(manager.execute(ScreenId.TRAY_SIZES,

            assertEquals(before, database.snapshot())

    private fun prepared(

        )).command

    private suspend fun withManager(block: suspend (ProductionScreenDataManager, LocalDatabase) -> Unit) {

        try {
            block(ProductionScreenDataManager(database, MultiplatformProductSettings(MapSettings())), database)
        } finally {
            database.close()

        }
    }

class StagePreviewStoreTest {
    @Test fun previewRequiresExplicitConfirmationAndAnyEditInvalidatesIt() = runTest {
        val manager = PreviewManager()
        val store = ScreenStoreProvider(DefaultStoreFactory(), manager, ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, "batch",
            UnconfinedTestDispatcher(testScheduler)).provide()
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.Submit(ScreenActionId("confirm-stage")))
        assertNotNull(store.state.stagePreview)
        assertTrue(manager.executed.isEmpty())
        assertEquals(0L, store.state.completionRevision)
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.EditField(ScreenFieldId("occurredAt"), "2026-10-11T12:00:00Z"))
        assertNull(store.state.stagePreview)
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.ConfirmStagePreview)
        assertTrue(manager.executed.isEmpty())
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.Submit(ScreenActionId("confirm-stage")))
        val reviewed = assertNotNull(store.state.stagePreview).command
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.ConfirmStagePreview)
        assertEquals(listOf(reviewed), manager.executed)
        assertNull(store.state.stagePreview)
        assertEquals(1L, store.state.completionRevision)
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.Execute(reviewed))
        assertEquals(1L, store.state.completionRevision, "A duplicate callback must not signal another completion")
        store.dispose()
    }

    @Test fun failedCommitRetainsReviewAndDoesNotSignalEditorCompletion() = runTest {
        val store = ScreenStoreProvider(DefaultStoreFactory(), PreviewManager(fail = true), ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL, "batch",
            UnconfinedTestDispatcher(testScheduler)).provide()
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.Submit(ScreenActionId("confirm-stage")))
        store.accept(ScreenStore.Intent.ConfirmStagePreview)
        assertNotNull(store.state.stagePreview)
        assertNotNull(store.state.errorKey)
        assertEquals(0L, store.state.completionRevision)
        store.dispose()
    }

    private class PreviewManager(private val fail: Boolean = false) : ScreenDataManager {
        val executed = mutableListOf<ScreenCommand>()
        private val snapshot = ScreenSnapshot(selectedItemId = "batch", fields =
            ScreenContractRegistry.contracts.getValue(ScreenId.BATCH_DETAIL).fields.map { field ->
                field.copy(value = when (field.id.value) {
                    "eventId" -> "event"
                    "occurredAt" -> "2026-10-10T12:00:00Z"
                    "nextState" -> "light_growth"
                    else -> ""
                })
            })
        override fun watch(screen: ScreenId, stableId: String?) = flowOf(snapshot)
        override suspend fun previewStage(command: ScreenCommand) = Result.success(StageChangeProjection(command, emptyList()))
        override suspend fun execute(screen: ScreenId, command: ScreenCommand): Result<ScreenSnapshot> {
            executed += command
            if (fail) return Result.failure(IllegalStateException("Cannot save"))
            return Result.success(snapshot)
        }
    }

internal fun stageTransition(batch: GrowBatch, command: ScreenCommand, placement: Placement): BatchChange {
    val event = StageEventId(command.required("eventId"))
    val occurredAt = command.instant("occurredAt")
    return when (command.operation) {
        "confirm-sowing" -> BatchLifecycleEngine.confirmSowing(batch, event, occurredAt, placement)
        "confirm-stage" -> BatchLifecycleEngine.confirmStage(batch, event, occurredAt, command.enum("nextState"), placement)
        "skip-stage" -> BatchLifecycleEngine.skipStage(batch, event, occurredAt, command.enum("skippedState"),
            command.required("reason"), command.enum("resultingState"))
        else -> error("Unsupported stage preview")
    }
}

internal fun BatchChange.preview(original: GrowBatch, command: ScreenCommand) = StageChangeProjection(
    command,
    batch.actions.filter { it.status == ScheduledActionStatus.PENDING }.map { action ->
        val previous = original.actions.firstOrNull { it.id == action.id }
        val conflict = conflicts.firstOrNull { it.actionId == action.id }
        StageDateChange(action.id.value, TextKey(when (action.stage) {
            GrowStage.SOAKING -> "stage_soaking"
            GrowStage.SOWN -> "stage_sown"
            GrowStage.BLACKOUT_OR_WEIGHT -> "stage_blackout"
            GrowStage.LIGHT_GROWTH -> "stage_light_growth"
            GrowStage.READY_FOR_HARVEST -> "stage_harvest"
            null -> "today_next_action"
        }), previous?.let(SchedulingEngine::resolvedInstant), SchedulingEngine.resolvedInstant(action), action.userFixed,
            conflict?.let { SchedulingEngine.resolvedInstant(action.copy(due = it.proposedDue)) })
    },
)

# Design

## Lazyweb evidence and direction

Lazyweb was consulted before screen selection.

Queries:

- `daily task dashboard` - strong adjacent evidence for Today hierarchy: current work first, concise status, stable bottom navigation, meaningful empty state.
- `plant growth tracker` - weak coverage; do not copy gamified "growth garden" or streak patterns.
- `harvest schedule planner` - adjacent planning evidence only; SproutPace uses a domain timeline rather than a generic calendar.
- `crop catalog cards` - weak coverage; use Material feed/grid semantics rather than treating results as validated microgreens patterns.
- Advertising research found no matching measured experiment. The qualitative [Agentic Search](https://www.lazyweb.com/agentic-search/2c55a632-370e-4a01-9e89-a6a5198460e8) supports clearly labeled inline browse/history placement and avoiding blocking promotional modals.

After implementation goldens exist, run first-release Lazyweb review over every primary screen and applicable light/dark/stress state. The post-golden report, not this preliminary search, is the implementation review evidence.

## Product expression

Use a calm botanical Material 3 system:

Brand update approved 2026-09-23: logo 1B-1 and palette A (Forest & Lime).
Light actions use forest green, dark actions use lime with dark-green content;
surface elevations, inverse colors and outlines use botanical neutrals. Native
icons preserve the full-color logo; in-app decorative marks retain semantic tint.
See `../docs/design-review/brand-refresh-20260923.md` for the approved mapping.

- warm neutral surfaces;
- green primary roles;
- restrained soil/gold tertiary accents;
- rounded, shallow-tray silhouettes and organic but readable illustration shapes;
- one hero moment on Today: the most important next action and capacity context;
- no streaks, mascots, confetti loops, diagnostic imagery, or novelty controls.

Prefer M3 Expressive variants when the repository's Compose Multiplatform version provides stable/accepted Android and iOS APIs. Otherwise use the semantically equivalent baseline Material 3 component and record the fallback. Do not custom-draw a missing expressive control merely to imitate its appearance.

## Navigation and adaptive layout

Primary destinations are stable:

1. Today
2. Trays
3. Plan
4. Catalog

Settings is a top-app-bar action, not a fifth primary destination.

| Width | Navigation | Content adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compact `<600dp` | Flexible/baseline navigation bar with icon + label | One pane; details navigate forward; 16dp semantic outer margin |
| Medium `600-839dp` | Collapsed navigation rail | One pane by default; optional supporting pane for Plan conflicts |
| Expanded `840-1199dp` | Collapsed/expanded navigation rail | List-detail for Trays, Catalog, Zones, and presets |
| Large `1200-1599dp` | Expanded navigation rail | Fixed list + flexible detail; Plan may show capacity supporting pane |
| Extra-large `>=1600dp` | Expanded navigation rail | Two panes by default; third pane only for a justified Plan conflict detail |

Each screen has one safe-area owner. Scaffold bars/rails own their corresponding inset; content consumes scaffold padding exactly once. Android predictive back and iOS back behavior map to the same platform-neutral navigation outputs.

## Screen inventory and hierarchy

| Screen | Primary task | Canonical layout | Highest-priority action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SCREEN-001 First run | Understand value or configure first cycle | Supporting pane / compact step flow | Continue setup or browse catalog |
| SCREEN-002 Today | Act on current and overdue work | Feed | Complete/open next action; New batch FAB when appropriate |
| SCREEN-003 Trays | Browse planned, active, and history | List-detail | New batch; open selected batch |
| SCREEN-004 Batch editor | Create/correct a batch | Form/supporting pane | Save/confirm batch |
| SCREEN-005 Batch detail | Understand state and record reality | Supporting pane | Confirm next actual stage |
| SCREEN-006 Plan | Edit cadence and resolve future conflicts | List-detail/supporting pane | Confirm suggestion or resolve conflict |
| SCREEN-007 Catalog | Browse built-in and personal recipes | Feed/grid | Open recipe; Create personal recipe |
| SCREEN-008 Recipe detail/editor | Read or edit recipe and sources | Supporting pane/form | Use recipe or Save personal recipe |
| SCREEN-009 Observation editor | Add/edit dated note and photo | Form | Save observation |
| SCREEN-010 Close batch | Record terminal outcome | Form/dialog on compact | Save outcome |
| SCREEN-011 Settings | Control product preferences/privacy/data | List | Contextual setting action |
| SCREEN-012 Zones | Manage capacity | List-detail | Add zone |
| SCREEN-013 Tray sizes | Manage reusable metric presets | List-detail | Add preset |
| SCREEN-014 Backup and restore | Export, preview, replace | List/supporting pane | Create backup or confirm restore |
| SCREEN-015 Advertising privacy | Make or change applicable consent | Full-screen decision on compact | Accept or decline; neither is visually deceptive |
| SCREEN-016 Notifications | Configure summary and permission recovery | Form/list | Enable/disable or change time |

## Material component map

- App framing: `Scaffold`, flexible/baseline top app bars, flexible/baseline navigation bar, collapsed/expanded navigation rail.
- Collections: standard/expressive lists, cards only where one subject and its actions form a coherent object; grids for catalog at wider sizes.
- Primary creation: one labeled extended FAB on Today/Trays when available; remove rather than disable when context makes it invalid.
- Actions: filled/tonal/outlined/text buttons by prominence; icon buttons only for familiar actions with localized semantics.
- Peer categories: primary tabs for Planned / Active / History within Trays. Tabs never represent sequential setup steps.
- Selection: radio buttons or connected button groups for zone type, tray shape, plan mode, and outcome; switches only for independent immediate settings such as Crashlytics and daily summary.
- Inputs: Material text fields with units/supporting text, date/time pickers with manual entry, and system photo/document pickers.
- Temporary decisions: basic dialog for irreversible delete/reset; bottom/side sheet for compact conflict explanation; persistent supporting pane at expanded widths.
- Feedback: actionable snackbars do not auto-dismiss; dialogs are reserved for decisions, not passive success.
- Progress/loading: show only for real database/file/network work. Core local screens prefer stable content/skeleton boundaries over decorative spinners.

## Today hierarchy

1. Page title and Settings action.
2. Hero next-action surface: action, tray/culture, due state, and one primary completion/open action.
3. Overdue actions.
4. Due today.
5. Next sow/harvest suggestion and capacity warning.
6. Calm empty state when no work exists; never replace it with a streak.

Completing a task provides an undo/review path where semantics permit. State is communicated with text/icon/shape as well as color.

## Stage and capacity presentation

Batch detail uses a vertical stage timeline with actual events, predicted windows, skipped markers, and the next action. Stage illustrations are decorative support and never diagnostic evidence.

Capacity is shown as named zones and occupied/available counts. Future conflicts use warning roles plus explicit text and actions: choose another date, choose/add a zone, change capacity, or retain `needs_resolution`. Actual overflow uses the same language but includes `Temporarily unassigned` so a user can record reality.

## Ads and privacy UI

Allowed slots only:

- SCREEN-007: one clearly labeled inline ad after the fourth culture card.
- SCREEN-003 History tab: one clearly labeled inline ad after the fifth historical record.

At most one ad is visible per eligible screen visit. No app-forced refresh loop is required. Ads are absent from short lists, empty/loading/error states, first run, Today, active batch detail, editors, stage confirmation, completion, planning decisions, settings, permissions, backup, and privacy.

No fill, offline, missing/stale eligibility, declined/unresolved consent, missing ID, SDK error, or iOS no-ID collapses the slot without blocking or leaving a misleading placeholder.

The app-owned protected-region consent screen appears at the first ad-eligible moment only when a fresh endpoint response requires it. It provides accept, decline, and privacy-policy actions with equal clarity. Non-protected responses show no global ad-consent popup or opt-out. Settings exposes withdrawal only while fresh applicability requires consent.
